title: Denying justification by inherent works does not deny true grace-wrought righteousness
source_text: XXIII. Proinde quum negant fideles justificari per opera, aut per ullam justitiam quae ipsis inhaereat, per id negare nolunt fidelibus inesse veri nominis justitiam, quam Deus per Christum gratam & acceptam habeat, ipsosque Dei gratia movente atque excitante, multos & varios fructus edere bonorum operum, quae Deus, juxta liberalem suam promissionem, coelesti & aeterna gloria remuneretur; sed eorum sententia est solummodo docere, nullam esse in fidelibus inhaerentem justitiam, nec ulla bona opera ab ipsis, etiam per Dei gratiam profecta, quae possint ferre rigidum & districtum examen divinae justitiae, si Deus velit cum ipsis in judicium intrare, absque clementia & misericordia: neque quenquam in Dei judicio absolvi posse, si Deus vitam & opera ejus severe discutiat, adeoque fideles coram Dei tribunali a peccati poenis, quas lex interminatur, absolvi, & immunes pronunciari, per meram Dei gratiam in Christo, non vero propter aliquam justitiam quae illis insit, ejusque merito atque intuitu.
pass_a_gloss: Therefore when they deny that the faithful are justified by works, or by any righteousness that inheres in them, by that they do not wish to deny that there is in the faithful a righteousness worthy of the name, which God through Christ holds grateful and accepted, and that they, God moving and exciting them by grace, bring forth many and various fruits of good works, which God, according to his liberal promise, will remunerate with heavenly and eternal glory; but their opinion is only to teach that there is no inherent righteousness in the faithful, nor any good works proceeding from them even by God's grace, which can bear the rigid and strict examination of divine justice, if God should wish to enter into judgment with them apart from clemency and mercy: nor can anyone be absolved in God's judgment if God severely examines his life and works; and so the faithful before God's tribunal are absolved from the penalties of sin which the law threatens, and pronounced immune, by the mere grace of God in Christ, not indeed because of any righteousness that is in them, and by its merit and regard.
pass_b_english: Denying justify-by-inherent-works does not deny real grace-wrought righteousness God accepts and rewards.
Point: no inherent work survives strict justice without mercy—acquittal is mere grace in Christ.

choices.why: Targets merit under strict justice, not fruit existence.
